# People: a real human figure and authored clips for the motion tests

The animation pipeline (#853) is judged on these files, not on the box man (`../gltf/humanoid.glb`), whose clips are generated by our own code. They are committed as test fixtures only. The repo ships importers, not game assets (#342), and this exception covers tests alone.

All three files are by Quaternius and are dedicated to the public domain under [CC0 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/).

| file | what it is | source | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mannequin.glb` | The male mannequin on the UE5 mannequin skeleton (65 joints, fingers and toes), with 43 clips from Universal Animation Library 2 Standard, among them `LayToIdle`, `Hit_Knockback`, `Walk_Carry_Loop` and idles. | `Unreal-Godot/UAL2_Standard.glb` in https://opengameart.org/content/universal-animation-library-2 (zip sha256 `ec0e40d6d78fe9aaad59e322f40865a8675c22f0745e291622e54520391a9217`) | `0815dd05531cae9bc313fc9c0ba81330bc72f8e19ec45f73738e74ddc5796a43` |
| `mannequin_f.glb` | The female mannequin on the same skeleton, with no clips. Clips are retargeted onto it. | `Female Mannequin/Unreal-Godot/Mannequin_F.glb` in the same zip | `2ee6cc3fe888d9b144afa8cc4b2ab7bfc5d13a0d5b7548df777f61f64ad65fa6` |
| `ual1_rigify.glb` | A mannequin on a Rigify-named skeleton (`DEF-hips`, `DEF-thigh.L`, 53 joints), with 46 clips from Universal Animation Library Standard: `Idle_Loop`, `Walk_Loop`, `Jog_Fwd_Loop`, `Sprint_Loop`, crouch, jumps, sitting, hits, death, roll, pistol and sword. | `Godot/AnimationLibrary_Godot_Standard.glb` in https://opengameart.org/sites/default/files/universal_animation_librarystandard.zip (zip sha256 `18ff1a7215f4852b320203e8aaf02a1578b5c8eef9027fbaedfcedc7b85a3ac2`) | `1b7bf67866360665426bb99e4c71bd619f19b408453c24e30f0c3071601eee5c` |

Each archive's `License.txt` reads: "CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication. Models by @Quaternius."

## A face: VRoid Studio's base female (`vroid_base_female.vrm`)

The face tests (`tests/test_face.ae`, #910) are judged on a figure with eye joints and blend shapes. It is VRoid Studio's base female model by pixiv's VRoid project, which VRoid released under [CC0 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/): VRoid's own page on its sample models' conditions of use (https://vroid.pixiv.help/hc/en-us/articles/4402614652569-Do-VRoid-Studio-s-sample-models-come-with-conditions-of-use) lists the base models among its "CC0 license models" ("Copyright is waived, and there is no particular limit when using them"). The file's own VRM metadata says the same: `"licenseName":"CC0"`, author "VRoidプロジェクト", redistribution and modification allowed. It is a VRM 0.x file, a glTF 2.0 binary, which `gltf.load` reads as any `.glb`.

| file | what it is | source | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vroid_base_female.vrm` | A figure of 83 joints on VRoid's skeleton (`J_Bip_C_Hips`, `J_Bip_L_UpperArm`... mapped as `pose.SCHEME_VROID`), with eye joints (`J_Adj_L_FaceEye`, `J_Adj_R_FaceEye`) and a face of 56 blend shapes in VRoid's own set (`Fcl_EYE_Close_L`, `Fcl_MTH_A`, `Fcl_ALL_Joy`...), not ARKit's 52: its eyes' closing is taken as ARKit's blinks (`face.shape_of`). Stripped of its pictures, 1.1 MB of the original's 16 MB (below). | `Base_Female.vrm` in https://opengameart.org/sites/default/files/base_female.zip (from https://opengameart.org/content/vroid-studio-cc0-models; zip sha256 `bf2717cff70b40a278df56e137dbb699c6499551096fa4c005e9aeca1de68eb3`; `Base_Female.vrm` sha256 `1995f174f6c8f2211f3c56c9e5fe4f9daf27ee5e648f129479582a259238149b`, 16,323,872 bytes) | `711313f9de3cc3bc84f73da56cad19e4dead20b2f87261b10aaacaefe258b8c1` (1,142,864 bytes) |

The committed file is the original made smaller by `tools/gltf_strip.ae`, with nothing the tests read changed:

    ./build.sh tools/gltf_strip.ae
    ./build/gltf_strip Base_Female.vrm tests/fixtures/people/vroid_base_female.vrm --sparse

It takes out the images, textures and samplers, the materials' and the VRM extension's references to them (the meta's thumbnail, MToon's texture properties) and the buffer views only the images used, and writes every morph target that moves fewer than three quarters of its vertices as a sparse accessor (the vertices it moves, their indices and values). The VRM metadata, the CC0 licence among it, is kept as it was. Loaded, the stripped file and the original agree on every vertex's place, normal, joints and weights and every morph target's offsets: 9,292,633 numbers, none different.

No face with ARKit's 52 blend shapes under CC0 or CC BY was found (2026-11-09): heads with the 52 offered for download are commercial or carry other terms (study-only, editorial-only), and the free ones in use in examples (three.js's `facecap.glb`) state no licence.

## 100STYLE: motion capture (`100style/`)

Cuts of the Neutral style of [the 100STYLE dataset](https://ianxmason.github.io/100style/) by Ian Mason, licensed under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/): "The 100STYLE Dataset - Ian Mason" (Mason, Starke and Komura, *Real-Time Style Modelling of Human Locomotion via Feature-Wise Transformations and Local Motion Phases*, 2022). The takes are Xsens inertial captures at 60 frames a second, in centimetres, of one actor walking and running around a capture volume for minutes at a time. Each locomotion file here is whole strides of one take, from a left footfall to a left footfall, where both the figure's travel and its hips keep their direction best (the stop and the start are where it comes to a stand and leaves it), cut by `tools/bvh_cut.ae`: the skeleton and the frames exactly as the dataset has them, and nothing else changed. The retargeter is held to them (`tests/test_anim_pipeline.ae`), and the blend spaces, starts, stops and turns are made from them.

The dataset's `100STYLE.zip` (Zenodo record 8127870, md5 `3cf627852fd8192024c04a8d0ef49583`), `100STYLE/Neutral/`:

## CMU: motion capture in its own format (`cmu/`)

One take from the [Carnegie Mellon University Motion Capture Database](http://mocap.cs.cmu.edu/), read in its own Acclaim ASF/AMC format by `bvh.load_asf` (#912) and held to a BVH conversion of the same take. The database's terms: "The data used in this project was obtained from mocap.cs.cmu.edu. The database was created with funding from NSF EIA-0196217." CMU places no restrictions on its use. Its takes are Vicon optical captures at 120 frames a second, in units of 1/0.45 inch (5.64 cm), angles in degrees.

The BVH is Bruce Hahne's conversion of the database (the cgspeed release, made with `amc2bvh`, its frame time set to 120/s), which adds no restrictions of its own. It is mirrored at https://github.com/meshula/cmu-mocap. It renames the bones (`LeftUpLeg` for `lfemur`), keeps the ASF's units and layout, and writes a rest frame before the take's first: its frame f + 1 is the AMC's frame f. It drops three bones' lengths: its neck joint sits on its thorax's, and each hand's finger and thumb joints on its wrist's.

| file | what it is | source | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `02.asf` | subject 02's skeleton: 30 bones, VICON BodyBuilder's layout | `http://mocap.cs.cmu.edu/subjects/02/02.asf` | `c9f5ff45b4437b279f58b95dacf017afd3135373096274df69436a9354d796cf` |
| `02_01.amc` | subject 02 walking, 343 frames | `http://mocap.cs.cmu.edu/subjects/02/02_01.amc` | `1503c481f4726e640c77888f0c841dd3be0694684bcd32296cf53685c6fc1492` |
| `02_01.bvh` | the same take converted to BVH, 344 frames | `data/002/02_01.bvh` in https://github.com/meshula/cmu-mocap | `cf56db43157acc3d200b3d4215523f54d354a8926bea67e1f6c8031bd335ba7e` |
| `02_05.amc.gz` | subject 02 punching and striking ("punch/strike"), 1854 frames, as the database has it, gzip'd (`gzip -9 -n`; `bvh.load_asf` inflates a `.gz`): the fight take the combat suite retargets (`tests/test_combat_takes.ae`, #907) | `http://mocap.cs.cmu.edu/subjects/02/02_05.amc` (sha256 `b370aae1972be9bf73d49a6c94ca74dda01a5cb5ab2f4cce7f61d4d08ca9a611`, 1,484,013 bytes) | `7526c82f7f8fcf2c9fafd6b47c7751dc057a4e31643c8d2d3129e5639bb1071e` |

The BVH conversion's names map onto the humanoid slots as the ASF's bones do (`pose.SCHEME_CMU`): `Spine` is the upper back, `Spine1` the thorax, `Neck` and `Neck1` the lower and upper neck, `LowerBack` and the hip joints left out as the ASF's are.
